items.sourceEnglish: Plant Selection & Guilds
items.draft: Ku Hlawula Swimilana ni Guilds
items.blindBackTranslation: Choosing Plants and Guilds

items.sourceEnglish: Choose useful plant partners, return mulch and manage the guild as trees grow.
items.draft: Hlawula swimilana swa vanghana leswi pfunaka, vuyisela mulch u tlhela u lawula guild loko minsinya yi ri karhi yi kula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose helpful friend plants, return mulch and manage the guild while the trees are growing.

items.sourceEnglish: These bacteria convert nitrogen from the air into forms the legume can use.
items.draft: Bakteriya (bacteria) leti ti hundzulula nitrogen leyi humaka emoyeni ku va swivumbeko leswi legume yi nga swi tirhisaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: These bacteria convert nitrogen that comes from the air into forms that the legume can use.

items.sourceEnglish: Find nodules on a spare legume plant. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, suitable bacteria and growing conditions.
items.draft: Kuma nodules eka ximilana xa legume lexi engetelekeke. Nodulation ni ku kula swi titshege hi ximilana, bakteriya (bacteria) leti faneleke ni swiyimo swa ku kula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Find nodules on an additional/extra legume plant. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, the suitable bacteria and the growing conditions.

items.sourceEnglish: Return suitable leafy prunings, fallen leaves and crop residues as mulch. Soil organisms release nutrients during decomposition.
items.draft: Vuyisela matluka lama tsemiweke lama faneleke, matluka lama wiseke ni masalela ya swilimiwa tanihi mulch. Swivumbiwa swa le misaveni swi humesa nutrients hi nkarhi wa decomposition.
items.blindBackTranslation: Return suitable cut leaves, fallen leaves and crop remains as mulch. Living things of the soil release nutrients during decomposition.

items.sourceEnglish: This takes time. A living legume is not an instant fertiliser pipe into the fruit tree.
items.draft: Leswi swi teka nkarhi. Legume leyi hanyaka a hi payiphi ya manyoro ya ku hatlisa leyi nghenaka eka nsinya wa mihandzu.
items.blindBackTranslation: This takes time. A living legume does not pay out quick manure that goes into the fruit tree.

items.sourceEnglish: It is indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage this short-lived shrub or small tree as a support plant.
items.draft: Yi indigenous eKwaZulu-Natal. Eka swiyimo leswi faneleke swa ku hisa, lawula xihlahla lexi kumbe nsinya lowutsongo lexi hanyaka nkarhi wo koma tanihi support plant.
items.blindBackTranslation: It is indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage this shrub or small short-lived tree as a support plant.

items.sourceEnglish: Allow room for its growth. Prune for mulch and reassess it when shade or water competition increases.
items.draft: Siya ndhawu yo kula ka yona. Tsema marhavi ya yona ku endla mulch u tlhela u yi kambisisa nakambe loko ndzhuti kumbe ku phikizana ka mati swi engeteleka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Leave a place for it to grow. Cut its branches to make mulch and check it again when shade or competition for water increases.

items.sourceEnglish: Sesbania punicea is the invasive red sesbania. Its pods have four lengthwise wings. Confirm identity using reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Sesbania punicea i red sesbania leyi invasive. Swikhwama swa yona swa mbewu (pods) swi ni tipapa ta mune leti leha hi ku leha ka xikhwama. Tiyisisa leswaku i xihi hi ku tirhisa botanical guidance leyi tshembekaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Sesbania punicea is the red sesbania that is invasive. Its seed pods have four wings, long along the length of the pod. Make sure which one it is by using trustworthy botanical guidance.

items.sourceEnglish: Check the full name before planting. Respect the agreed project species list, including any restriction on Sesbania sesban.
items.draft: Kambisisa vito hinkwaro ku nga si byala. Xixima project species list leyi pfumeleriweke, ku katsa ni nsivelo wihi na wihi eka Sesbania sesban.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the full name before planting. Respect the approved project species list, including any restriction on Sesbania sesban.

items.sourceEnglish: Use a sunny, freely draining position. It is a short-lived support shrub; frost and waterlogging can limit it.
items.draft: Tirhisa ndhawu leyi nga ni dyambu laha mati ma khulukaka kahle. I support shrub leyi hanyaka nkarhi wo koma; frost ni ku yima ka mati emisaveni swi nga yi hunguta ku kula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Use a place that has sun where water drains well. It is a support shrub that lives a short time; frost and standing water in the soil can reduce its growth.

items.sourceEnglish: Decide whether each plant mainly supplies peas or leafy material. Frequent severe cutting can damage it and reduce the food harvest.
items.draft: Endla xiboho xana ximilana xin'wana ni xin'wana xi ta nyika ngopfu tiphizi kumbe matluka. Ku tsema ku vuyeriwa ni ku tika swi nga xi onha, swi tlhela swi hunguta ntshovelo wa swakudya.
items.blindBackTranslation: Do not let every plant [?] give a lot of tiphizi [?] or leaves. Pruning that is [?] done again and [?] done again, can harm them, and also reduces the harvest of food. (Note: 'Endla' read as 'don't let / do not allow' [?]; 'tiphizi' unknown, possibly 'pieces/branches' [?]; 'ku tsema ku vuyeriwa' = 'cutting that is returned/repeated' [?]; 'ku tika' = 'to break/damage' [?]; 'swi nga xi onha' = 'it can damage it'.)

items.sourceEnglish: Cowpea covers sunny gaps. Pigeon pea provides food and leafy material. Managed Sesbania sesban can supply taller temporary support.
items.draft: Cowpea yi funengeta tindhawu to pfula leti nga ni dyambu. Pigeon pea yi nyika swakudya ni matluka. Sesbania sesban leyi lawuriweke yi nga nyika support plant leyi leheleke ya nkarhi wo koma.
items.blindBackTranslation: Cowpea covers open places that have sun. Pigeon pea gives food and leaves. A managed Sesbania sesban can give a tall short-lived support plant.

items.sourceEnglish: Add suitable flowering and mulch plants. Keep the mango trunk clear and manage light, water and access.
items.draft: Engetela swimilana leswi faneleke leswi nga ni swiluva ni swimilana swa mulch. Hlayisa xidzimba xa nsinya wa mango xi pfulekile, u lawula dyambu, mati ni ndlela yo nghena.
items.blindBackTranslation: Add suitable plants that have flowers, and mulch plants. Keep the base/trunk area of the mango tree open, and control sun, water and access/way in.

items.sourceEnglish: Count woody supports across the spaces between fruit trees. Sow suitable ground cover by area.
items.draft: Hlaya support plants leti tiyeke ku fana ni minsinya, leti nga eka tindhawu hinkwato exikarhi ka minsinya ya mihandzu. Byala swimilana leswi faneleke swo funengeta misava hi ku ya hi vukulu bya ndhawu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose support plants that are strong, like trees [?], that are in all places in between the fruit trees. Plant suitable plants to cover the soil according to the size of the area.

items.sourceEnglish: There is no universal number per fruit tree. Adjust density to water, soil, plant size and your ability to prune and thin.
items.draft: A ku na nhlayo yin'we leyi tirhaka hinkwako eka nsinya wa mihandzu wun'wana ni wun'wana. Cinca support density hi ku ya hi mati, misava, vukulu bya swimilana ni vuswikoti bya wena bya ku tsema ni ku endla thinning.
items.blindBackTranslation: There is no one number that works everywhere for every fruit tree. Change the support density according to water, soil, the size of the plants and your ability to cut and to do thinning.

items.sourceEnglish: Conceptual guild teaching illustration; confirm plant identity with reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Xifaniso xa ku dyondzisa lexi kombisaka mianakanyo ya guild; tiyisisa leswaku i ximilana xihi hi ku tirhisa botanical guidance leyi tshembekaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Teaching picture that shows guild ideas; make sure which plant it is by using botanical guidance that is trustworthy.

items.sourceEnglish: Nitrogen Fixers: Choose and Manage Support Plants
items.draft: Nitrogen Fixers: Hlawula ni ku Lawula Support Plants
items.blindBackTranslation: Nitrogen Fixers: Choosing and Managing Support Plants

items.sourceEnglish: Legumes work with rhizobia in root nodules; fixation depends on suitable conditions.
items.draft: Legumes ti tirha ni rhizobia eka nodules ya timitsu; nitrogen fixation yi titshege hi swiyimo leswi faneleke.
items.blindBackTranslation: Legumes work with rhizobia in the nodules of the roots; nitrogen fixation depends on suitable conditions.

items.sourceEnglish: Return useful cut material to the soil; nutrient release takes time.
items.draft: Vuyisela swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi pfunaka emisaveni; ku humesiwa ka nutrients ku teka nkarhi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Return the cut things that help to the soil; the release of nutrients takes time.

items.sourceEnglish: Use suitable seasonal cover, support shrubs and temporary trees.
items.draft: Tirhisa swimilana leswi faneleke swo funengeta swa minkarhi ya lembe, support shrubs ni minsinya ya nkarhi wo koma.
items.blindBackTranslation: Use suitable plants for covering the soil of the seasons of the year, support shrubs and trees of short time.

items.sourceEnglish: Manage support density as plants grow; there is no universal count per fruit tree.
items.draft: Lawula support density loko swimilana swi ri karhi swi kula; a ku na nhlayo yin'we leyi tirhaka hinkwako eka nsinya wa mihandzu wun'wana ni wun'wana.
items.blindBackTranslation: Manage support density while the plants are growing; there is no one number that works everywhere for every fruit tree.

items.sourceEnglish: When does nitrogen in cut legume material become available to other plants?
items.draft: Nitrogen leyi nga eka swilo swa legume leswi tsemiweke yi kumeka rini eka swimilana swin'wana?
items.blindBackTranslation: When is the nitrogen that is in the cut legume things found in some plants?

items.sourceEnglish: Immediately when it is cut
items.draft: Hi ku hatlisa loko yi tsemiwa
items.blindBackTranslation: Quickly when it is cut

items.sourceEnglish: As soil organisms decompose the material
items.draft: Loko swivumbiwa swa le misaveni swi endla decomposition ya swilo leswi
items.blindBackTranslation: When the living things of the soil do decomposition of these things

items.sourceEnglish: Only when the fruit tree touches the legume
items.draft: Ntsena loko nsinya wa mihandzu wu khumba legume
items.blindBackTranslation: Only when the fruit tree touches the legume

items.sourceEnglish: It can never become available
items.draft: A yi nge he yi kumeka nikatsongo
items.blindBackTranslation: It will never be found at all

items.sourceEnglish: Decomposition releases nutrients over time. The rate depends on the material and growing conditions.
items.draft: Decomposition yi humesa nutrients hi ku famba ka nkarhi. Ku hatlisa ka kona ku titshege hi swilo leswi swi volaka ni swiyimo swa ku kula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Decomposition releases nutrients over time. How fast it is depends on the things that rot and on the growing conditions.

items.sourceEnglish: What should decide how many support plants you establish?
items.draft: I yini leyi faneleke ku endla xiboho xa nhlayo ya support plants leyi u yi byalaka?
items.blindBackTranslation: What must make the decision of the number of support plants that you plant?

items.sourceEnglish: The same fixed number at every site
items.draft: Nhlayo yin'we leyi nga cinciki eka ndhawu yin'wana ni yin'wana
items.blindBackTranslation: One number that does not change in every place

items.sourceEnglish: Water, soil, plant size and the care you can provide
items.draft: Mati, misava, vukulu bya swimilana ni ku khathalela loku u kotaka ku ku endla
items.blindBackTranslation: Water, soil, size of the plants and the care that you are able to do

items.sourceEnglish: Always placing every support uphill
items.draft: Minkarhi hinkwayo ku veka support plant yin'wana ni yin'wana endhawini leyi nga ehenhla loko u tlhandlukela
items.blindBackTranslation: Always, to put each support plant in a place that is above when you go uphill

items.sourceEnglish: Planting as many trees as will physically fit
items.draft: Ku byala minsinya yo tala hilaha ndhawu yi nga yi kotaka hakona
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant many trees as much as the place is able to

items.sourceEnglish: Support plants need resources and management too. Observe growth and competition, then adjust.
items.draft: Support plants na tona ti lava swipfuno ni ku lawuriwa. Languta ku kula ni ku phikizana, kutani u cinca.
items.blindBackTranslation: Support plants also need resources and to be managed. Watch growth and competition, then change.

items.sourceEnglish: The clip shows a branch cut: the support tree remains standing. Leave enough healthy foliage for the plant to recover.
items.draft: Vhidiyo yi kombisa ku tsemiwa ka rhavi: support tree yi sala yi yimile. Siya matluka lama hanyaka lama ringaneke leswaku ximilana xi vuya xi hanya.
items.blindBackTranslation: The video shows the cutting of a branch: the support tree remains standing. Leave enough living leaves so that the plant recovers and lives.

items.sourceEnglish: Match cutting to the species. Avoid frequent severe cuts on pigeon pea, especially when growing it for peas.
items.draft: Fambisana ku tsema ni muxaka wa ximilana. Papalata ku tsema ku vuyeriwa ni ku tika eka pigeon pea, ngopfu-ngopfu loko u yi byala ku kuma tinyawa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Match the cutting with the type of plant. Avoid cutting that is repeated and heavy on pigeon pea, especially when you plant it to get seeds [?: 'tinyawa' read as beans/peas].

items.sourceEnglish: Mulch protects the surface, helps conserve moisture and returns organic material.
items.draft: Mulch yi sirhelela misava ya le henhla, yi pfuna ku hlayisa ku nyama ka misava naswona yi vuyisela swilo leswi humaka eka swilo leswi hanyaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Mulch protects the top soil, helps to keep the moisture of the soil, and returns things that come from living things.

items.sourceEnglish: Leave access for watering and inspection. Cut material into manageable pieces and keep observing moisture and decomposition.
items.draft: Siya ndlela yo nghena ku cheleta mati ni ku kambisisa. Tsema swilo swi va swiphemu leswi swi nga khomekaka, u tlhela u ya emahlweni u languta ku nyama ni decomposition.
items.blindBackTranslation: Leave a way in for watering and checking. Cut things into pieces that can be handled, and go ahead watching for moisture and decomposition.

items.sourceEnglish: Obtain the correct cultivar. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but root pieces can regrow.
items.draft: Kuma cultivar leyi lulameke. Bocking 14 a yi hangalaki hi viable seed, kambe swiphemu swa timitsu swi nga ha mila nakambe.
items.blindBackTranslation: Find a cultivar that is right. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but pieces of roots may grow again.

items.sourceEnglish: Place it where it has room and sufficient moisture. Cut leaves as it recovers; do not crowd the young fruit tree.
items.draft: Yi veke laha yi nga ni ndhawu ni ku nyama ka misava loku ringaneke. Tsema matluka loko yi ri karhi yi vuya yi hanya; u nga yi byali ekusuhi swinene ni nsinya lowutsongo wa mihandzu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Put it where it has space and moderate wetness of the soil. Cut the leaves while it is busy coming back to life/recovering; do not plant it very close to a small fruit tree.

items.sourceEnglish: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack crop pests. Flowering members such as African basil can add resources.
items.draft: Ladybirds yo tala ti dya aphids; parasitoid wasps tin'wana ti hlasela swinyenyana leswi onhaka swilimiwa (pests). Swimilana leswi nga ni swiluva ku fana ni African basil swi nga engetela swipfuno.
items.blindBackTranslation: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack insects that damage crops. Plants that have flowers like African basil can add resources.

items.sourceEnglish: Watch which insects visit and whether damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee pest control.
items.draft: Languta swinyenyana (insects) leswi endzelaka ni loko ku onhaka ku cinca. Ximilana lexi nga ni swiluva a xi tiyisekisi ku lawula swinyenyana leswi onhaka (pests).
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch the insects that visit and whether the damage changes. A plant that has flowers does not guarantee control of insects that damage.

items.sourceEnglish: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac flowers. Place a clump where it has light and room to grow.
items.draft: Tulbaghia violacea yi ni matluka lama ndzhonga ni swiluva swa lilac. Veka xihlopha xa yona laha xi nga ni dyambu ni ndhawu yo kula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow/thin leaves and lilac flowers. Put its group/clump where it has sun and space to grow.

items.sourceEnglish: Observe visiting insects. Do not promise that a ring of wild garlic will repel pests or cure an outbreak.
items.draft: Languta swinyenyana (insects) leswi endzelaka. U nga tshembisi leswaku xirhendzevutani xa wild garlic xi ta hlongola swinyenyana leswi onhaka (pests) kumbe ku herisa ku hangalaka ka swona.
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch the insects that visit. Do not promise that a wild garlic circle [?: 'xirhendzevutani' read as a ring/border] will chase away the insects that damage or end their spreading.

items.sourceEnglish: Conceptual guild teaching illustration; confirm plant identity with reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Xifaniso xa ku dyondzisa lexi kombisaka mianakanyo ya guild; tiyisisa leswaku i ximilana xihi hi ku tirhisa botanical guidance leyi tshembekaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Teaching picture that shows guild ideas; make sure which plant it is by using botanical guidance that is trustworthy.

items.sourceEnglish: Mulch Plants and Helpful Insects
items.draft: Swimilana swa Mulch ni Swinyenyana (insects) swo Pfuna
items.blindBackTranslation: Mulch Plants and Helpful Insects

items.sourceEnglish: Pruning cuts branches while keeping the support plant.
items.draft: Ku tsema marhavi swi vula ku tsema marhavi ya support plant ku ri karhi yi hlayisiwa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Cutting branches means cutting the branches of a support plant while it is kept/preserved [i.e. the plant is kept alive].

items.sourceEnglish: Return suitable cut leaves as mulch while keeping the trunk clear.
items.draft: Vuyisela matluka lama tsemiweke lama faneleke tanihi mulch, u siya xidzimba xa nsinya xi nga ni nchumu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Return suitable cut leaves as mulch, leaving the bare ground of the tree [?] empty.

items.sourceEnglish: Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but root pieces can regrow.
items.draft: Bocking 14 a yi hangalaki hi viable seed, kambe swiphemu swa timitsu swi nga ha mila nakambe.
items.blindBackTranslation: Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but pieces of roots may grow again.

items.sourceEnglish: Flowering plants can support useful insects; watch actual visits and crop damage.
items.draft: Swimilana leswi nga ni swiluva swi nga pfuna swinyenyana (insects) swo pfuna; languta leswi swi endzelaka hakunene ni ku onhaka ka swilimiwa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plants that have flowers may help helpful small creatures [insects?] [?]; watch which ones really visit and the damaging of crops.

items.sourceEnglish: What does the branch-cutting clip show?
items.draft: Vhidiyo ya ku tsema rhavi yi kombisa yini?
items.blindBackTranslation: What does the video of cutting a branch show?

items.sourceEnglish: Removing the whole support tree
items.draft: Ku susa support tree hinkwayo
items.blindBackTranslation: Removing the whole support tree

items.sourceEnglish: Pruning a retained support tree for light and mulch
items.draft: Ku tsema marhavi ya support tree leyi hlayisiweke ku kuma dyambu ni mulch
items.blindBackTranslation: Cutting the branches of a support tree that is kept, to get sun and mulch

items.sourceEnglish: Harvesting the fruit tree
items.draft: Ku tshovela nsinya wa mihandzu
items.blindBackTranslation: Harvesting a fruit tree

items.sourceEnglish: Proof that root competition has stopped
items.draft: Vumbhoni bya leswaku ku phikizana ka timitsu ku herile
items.blindBackTranslation: Evidence that competition of roots has ended

items.sourceEnglish: A branch falls, while the support tree remains standing. That is pruning and chop-and-drop.
items.draft: Rhavi ri wa, kasi support tree yi sala yi yimile. Leswi hi ku tsema marhavi ni chop-and-drop.
items.blindBackTranslation: A branch falls, while the support tree remains standing. This is by cutting of branches and chop-and-drop.

items.sourceEnglish: How should you assess flowering plants used to support helpful insects?
items.draft: U fanele ku kambisisa njhani swimilana leswi nga ni swiluva leswi tirhisiwaka ku pfuna swinyenyana (insects) swo pfuna?
items.blindBackTranslation: How must you check plants that have flowers that are used to help helpful insects?

items.sourceEnglish: Assume they will eliminate pests
items.draft: Ku ehleketa leswaku swi ta herisa swinyenyana leswi onhaka (pests)
items.blindBackTranslation: To think that they will end the insects that damage

items.sourceEnglish: Observe insect visitors and changes in crop damage
items.draft: Languta swinyenyana (insects) leswi endzelaka ni ku cinca ka ku onhaka ka swilimiwa
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch the insects that visit and the change of damage of crops

items.sourceEnglish: Remove all flowers before they open
items.draft: Susa swiluva hinkwaswo swi nga si pfuleka
items.blindBackTranslation: Remove all the flowers before they open

items.sourceEnglish: Count every flowering plant as a nitrogen fixer
items.draft: Hlaya ximilana xin'wana ni xin'wana lexi nga ni swiluva tanihi nitrogen fixer
items.blindBackTranslation: Count each plant that has flowers as a nitrogen fixer

items.sourceEnglish: Flowers can supply resources, but their presence does not guarantee pest control.
items.draft: Swiluva swi nga nyika swipfuno, kambe ku va kona ka swona a ku tiyisekisi ku lawula swinyenyana leswi onhaka (pests).
items.blindBackTranslation: Flowers can give resources, but their being there does not guarantee control of insects that damage.

items.sourceEnglish: Combine the support functions your site needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground cover. Some plants serve several functions.
items.draft: Hlanganisa support functions leswi ndhawu ya wena yi swi lavaka: nitrogen fixation, swakudya, mulch, swiluva ni swimilana swo funengeta misava. Swimilana swin'wana swi tirha mintirho yo hlayanyana.
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine the support functions that your place needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and plants for covering soil. Some plants do several jobs.

items.sourceEnglish: Keep the trunk area and path open. Reassess each member as the mango and its neighbours grow.
items.draft: Siyisani ndhawu leyi rhendzeleke nsinya ni ndlela swi pfulekile. Tlhela u kambisisa ximilana xin'wana ni xin'wana loko mango ni swimilana leswi nga ekusuhi swi ri karhi swi kula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Leave the place that surrounds the tree and the way in open. Check again each plant when the mango and the plants that are nearby are growing.

items.sourceEnglish: Keep its vines away from the young fruit tree and retain a route for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients.
items.draft: Hlayisa marhavi ya yona lama hangalaka emisaveni ma ri ekule ni nsinya lowutsongo wa mihandzu, u tlhela u siya ndlela ya ku khathalela. Timitsu ta yona na tona ti tirhisa mati ni nutrients.
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep its branches that spread out on the ground, being far from the small fruit tree, and also leave a way to take care of it. Its roots also use water and nutrients. (Note: 'u tlhela u siya ndlela ya ku khathalela' = 'and also leave a path for caring/tending'.)

items.sourceEnglish: Where resources are tight, compare living cover with an ordinary mulch basin.
items.draft: Laha swipfuno swi nga ringanangiki, pimanisa swimilana leswi funengetaka misava leswi hanyaka ni mulch basin ya ntolovelo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Where resources are not enough, compare the plants that cover the soil that live with the ordinary mulch basin.

items.sourceEnglish: Plant into a suitable season, mulch and maintain establishment water. Keep the access gap open.
items.draft: Byala hi nkarhi lowu faneleke, veka mulch u tlhela u hlayisa ku cheleta mati hi nkarhi wo sungula ku mila endzhaku ka ku byala (establishment). Siya ndhawu yo nghena yi pfulekile.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant at a suitable time, put mulch and keep watering at the early time of growth after planting. Leave the place of access open.

items.sourceEnglish: Start with the number of support plants you can care for. Observe survival and growth before adding more.
items.draft: Sungula hi nhlayo ya support plants leyi u nga kotaka ku yi khathalela. Languta ku hanya ni ku kula ku nga si engetela swin'wana.
items.blindBackTranslation: Start with a number of support plants that you can care for. Watch survival and growth before adding others.

items.sourceEnglish: Cut down selected competing supports to open space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning through chop-and-drop.
items.draft: Tsema ehansi support plants leti phikizanaka leti hlawuriweke ku pfula ndhawu. Swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi faneleke swi nga sala tanihi mulch: leswi i thinning hi chop-and-drop.
items.blindBackTranslation: Cut down competing support plants that are chosen to open space. Suitable cut things can remain as mulch: this is thinning by chop-and-drop.

items.sourceEnglish: Manage regrowth to keep the opening. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning does not instantly stop root competition.
items.draft: Lawula ku mila nakambe ku hlayisa ndhawu leyi pfuleke. Kambisisa dyambu, ku nyama ka misava ni ku kula; thinning a yi herisi hi xihatla ku phikizana ka timitsu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Control the growing again to keep the place open. Check sun, wetness of the soil and growth; thinning does not end root competition quickly.

items.sourceEnglish: Carry useful prunings back to established trees. Keep nearby plants only where they still perform well.
items.draft: Tlherisela swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi pfunaka eka minsinya leyi se yi tiyeke kahle emisaveni. Hlayisa swimilana leswi nga ekusuhi laha ntsena swi ha tirhaka kahle.
items.blindBackTranslation: Return the cut things that help to trees that are already well established in the soil. Keep plants that are nearby only where they still work well.

items.sourceEnglish: Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Monitor growth, harvest and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need.
items.draft: Minsinya ya mihandzu leyi kuleke yi ha lava nutrients. Languta ku kula, ntshovelo ni swiyimo swa misava; support plants a swi susi xilaveko lexi.
items.blindBackTranslation: Fruit trees that have grown still need nutrients. Watch growth, harvest and the state of the soil; support plants do not remove this need.

items.sourceEnglish: Check fruit-tree growth, shade, soil moisture, useful harvests and pest damage. Note what was cut, returned or removed.
items.draft: Kambisisa ku kula ka nsinya wa mihandzu, ndzhuti, ku nyama ka misava, ntshovelo wo pfuna ni ku onhiwa hi swinyenyana leswi onhaka (pests). Tsala leswi tsemiweke, leswi tlheriseriweke kumbe leswi susiweke.
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the growth of the fruit tree, shade, moisture of the soil, helpful harvest and damage by insects that damage. Write down what was cut, what was returned or what was removed.

items.sourceEnglish: Use these observations to change the layout and care. A plant earns its place through what it does here.
items.draft: Tirhisa leswi u swi voneke ku cinca ndlela leyi swimilana swi vekiwaka ha yona ni ndlela leyi u swi khathalelaka ha yona. Ximilana xi kuma ndhawu ya xona hi leswi xi swi endlaka laha.
items.blindBackTranslation: Use what you have seen to change the way plants are placed and the way you care for them. A plant finds its place by what it does here.

items.sourceEnglish: Conceptual guild teaching illustration; confirm plant identity with reliable botanical guidance.
items.draft: Xifaniso xa ku dyondzisa lexi kombisaka mianakanyo ya guild; tiyisisa leswaku i ximilana xihi hi ku tirhisa botanical guidance leyi tshembekaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Teaching picture that shows guild ideas; make sure which plant it is by using botanical guidance that is trustworthy.

items.sourceEnglish: Build a Guild and Adjust It as It Grows
items.draft: Aka Guild u yi Cinca Loko yi Ri Karhi yi Kula
items.blindBackTranslation: Build the Guild and Change It While It Is Growing

items.sourceEnglish: Give each plant a useful role while protecting the fruit tree's space.
items.draft: Nyika ximilana xin'wana ni xin'wana ntirho wo pfuna, u ri karhi u sirhelela ndhawu ya nsinya wa mihandzu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Give each plant a helping job, while protecting the place of the fruit tree.

items.sourceEnglish: Living ground cover also competes for water and nutrients.
items.draft: Swimilana leswi funengetaka misava leswi hanyaka na swona swi phikizana ku kuma mati ni nutrients.
items.blindBackTranslation: Living plants that cover the soil also compete to get water and nutrients.

items.sourceEnglish: Thin selected whole support plants when pruning no longer gives enough room.
items.draft: Endla thinning hi ku susa hi ku helela support plants leti hlawuriweke loko ku tsema marhavi ku nga ha nyiki ndhawu leyi ringaneke.
items.blindBackTranslation: Do thinning by removing completely the support plants that were chosen when cutting branches does not give enough space.

items.sourceEnglish: Suitable cut biomass can stay as mulch; manage regrowth to retain the opening.
items.draft: Biomass leyi tsemiweke leyi faneleke yi nga sala tanihi mulch; lawula ku mila nakambe ku hlayisa ndhawu leyi pfuleke.
items.blindBackTranslation: Biomass that is cut that is suitable can remain as mulch; manage regrowth to keep the open place.

items.sourceEnglish: A support plant still crowds the mango after pruning. What can thinning involve?
items.draft: Support plant yi ha phikizana ni mango endzhaku ka ku tsema marhavi. Thinning yi nga katsa yini?
items.blindBackTranslation: A support plant is still competing with the mango after cutting of branches. What can thinning include?

items.sourceEnglish: Only cutting another small twig
items.draft: Ku tsema ntsena rhavi rin'wana ro tsongo
items.blindBackTranslation: Cutting only one small branch

items.sourceEnglish: Cutting down a selected competing support and managing regrowth
items.draft: Ku tsema ehansi support plant leyi phikizanaka leyi hlawuriweke ni ku lawula ku mila nakambe
items.blindBackTranslation: Cutting down the competing support plant that is chosen and managing regrowth

items.sourceEnglish: Removing the mango instead
items.draft: Ku susa mango ematshan'wini ya sweswo
items.blindBackTranslation: Removing the mango instead of that

items.sourceEnglish: Always carrying all cut biomass off the site
items.draft: Minkarhi hinkwayo ku rhwala biomass hinkwayo leyi tsemiweke u yi susa endhawini
items.blindBackTranslation: Always carrying all the biomass that is cut and removing it from the place

items.sourceEnglish: Thinning reduces selected standing support plants. Suitable cut material may stay as mulch.
items.draft: Thinning yi hunguta support plants leti yimeke leti hlawuriweke. Swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi faneleke swi nga sala tanihi mulch.
items.blindBackTranslation: Thinning reduces support plants that are standing that are chosen. Suitable cut things can remain as mulch.

items.sourceEnglish: Is sweet potato always better than a mulch basin around a young fruit tree?
items.draft: Xana sweet potato minkarhi hinkwayo yi antswa ku tlula mulch basin leyi rhendzeleke nsinya lowutsongo wa mihandzu?
items.blindBackTranslation: Is sweet potato always better than the mulch basin that surrounds the small fruit tree?

items.sourceEnglish: Yes, because it never uses water
items.draft: Ina, hikuva a yi tirhisi mati nikatsongo
items.blindBackTranslation: Yes, because it does not use any water

items.sourceEnglish: Yes, because it fixes nitrogen
items.draft: Ina, hikuva yi endla nitrogen fixation
items.blindBackTranslation: Yes, because it does nitrogen fixation

items.sourceEnglish: No; compare its food and cover benefits with competition for resources
items.draft: Ee-e; pimanisa vuyelo bya swakudya ni ku funengeta loku yi ku nyikaka ni ku phikizana ka swipfuno
items.blindBackTranslation: No; compare the result of food and the covering that it gives and the competition of resources [?]

items.sourceEnglish: No, because no ground cover can ever be useful
items.draft: Ee-e, hikuva a ku na ximilana xo funengeta misava lexi nga pfunaka nikatsongo
items.blindBackTranslation: No, because there is no plant for covering the soil that helps even a little

items.sourceEnglish: Choose cover for the site. Keep access and the trunk area clear, and observe the young tree.
items.draft: Hlawula swimilana swo funengeta leswi faneleke ndhawu. Hlayisa ndhawu yo nghena ni ndhawu ya xidzimba xi nga ni nchumu, u languta nsinya lowutsongo.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose plants for covering that are suitable for the place. Keep the place of access and the place of bare ground [?] empty, watching the small tree.

items.sourceEnglish: Plant Selection and Guilds
items.draft: Ku Hlawula Swimila na Guilds
items.blindBackTranslation: Choosing Plants and Guilds

items.sourceEnglish: Choose plants that work together—and change the planting as it grows.
items.draft: Hlawula swimila leswi tirhaka swin'we—kutani u cinca ku byala loko swi ya swi kula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose plants that work together—and then change the planting as they keep growing.

items.sourceEnglish: Plant Selection and Guilds
items.draft: Ku Hlawula Swimila na Guilds
items.blindBackTranslation: Choosing Plants and Guilds

items.sourceEnglish: A fruit tree needs light, water, soil nutrients and room. Support plants can supply food, leafy mulch, flowers and living cover.  Give each plant a useful job. Keep observing whether it helps the tree and the household. Which jobs does your planting need?
items.draft: Murhi wa mihandzu wu lava ku vonakala, mati, nutrients ta misava ni ndhawu. Support plants swi nga nyika swakudya, mulch wa matluka, swiluva ni xifunengeto xa swimila leswi hanyaka. Nyika ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana ntirho lowu pfunaka. Tshama u langutisisa leswaku xana xi pfuna murhi ni ndyangu. Hi tihi tintirho leti ku byala ka wena ku ti lavaka?
items.blindBackTranslation: A fruit tree needs light/sunshine, water, nutrients of the soil and space. Support plants can give food, leaf mulch, flowers and a covering of living plants. Give each plant a helpful job. Always observe closely whether it helps the tree and the family [?: ndyangu = family/household]. Which jobs does your planting need?

items.sourceEnglish: Start With the Site
items.draft: Sungula Hi Ndhawu
items.blindBackTranslation: Start With the Site

items.sourceEnglish: Find out what is limiting growth before choosing a plant.
items.draft: Kuma leswi hungutaka ku kula u nga si hlawula ximila.
items.blindBackTranslation: Find what reduces growth before you choose a plant.

items.sourceEnglish: Start With the Site
items.draft: Sungula Hi Ndhawu
items.blindBackTranslation: Start With the Site

items.sourceEnglish: Check sunlight, drainage, soil condition and water availability. Nitrogen is only one possible limitation.  Compare the soil beneath mulch with exposed soil. Choose support plants that fit the actual conditions. What does this site need first?
items.draft: Languta ku vonakala ka dyambu, ndlela leyi mati ma hundzaka ha yona ekhatsi ka misava, xiyimo xa misava ni leswaku mati ma kona. Nitrogen i xin'wana ntsena xa swilo leswi nga ha hungutaka ku kula. Fananisa misava leyi nga ehansi ka mulch ni misava leyi nga funeriwangiki. Hlawula support plants leswi fambisanaka ni swiyimo leswi nga kona hakunene. Xana ndhawu leyi yi sungula yi lava yini?
items.blindBackTranslation: Look at how the sun shows/appears [?], the way water passes through inside the soil, the condition of the soil, and whether water is present. Nitrogen is only one of the things that can decrease growth [?: 'ku hungutaka ku kula' = decrease growing]. Compare the soil that is under mulch and soil that is not covered. Choose support plants that fit together with the conditions that are really there. What does this place begin by needing?

items.sourceEnglish: Give Every Plant a Job
items.draft: Nyika Ximila Xin'wana Ni Xin'wana Ntirho
items.blindBackTranslation: Give Each Plant a Job

items.sourceEnglish: A useful guild produces benefits you can observe.
items.draft: Guild leyi pfunaka yi humesa mimpfuno leyi u nga yi vonaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: A guild that helps produces benefits that you can see.

items.sourceEnglish: Give Every Plant a Job
items.draft: Nyika Ximila Xin'wana Ni Xin'wana Ntirho
items.blindBackTranslation: Give Each Plant a Job

items.sourceEnglish: Choose members for food, nitrogen fixation, mulch, flowers or ground cover. One plant may do several jobs.  By the end, plan a guild, explain how residues feed soil, and decide which support plants to keep, cut or remove. Which job is still missing?
items.draft: Hlawula swirho swa guild ku va swakudya, nitrogen fixation, mulch, swiluva kumbe ku funengeta misava. Ximila xin'we xi nga endla mintirho yo tala. Eku heleni, hlela guild, hlamusela ndlela leyi swisaleli swi phamelaka misava swakudya ha yona, u tlhela u endla xiboho xa leswaku hi swihi support plants leswi u nga ta ku swi hlayisa, ku swi tsema kumbe ku swi susa. Hi wihi ntirho lowu ha pfumalaka?
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose guild members to be food, nitrogen fixation, mulch, flowers or covering the soil. One plant can do many jobs. At the end, plan the guild, explain the way the plants feed the soil, and also make a decision about which support plants you will keep, prune or remove. Which job is still lacking?

items.sourceEnglish: Look for Root Nodules
items.draft: Lava Nodules eka Timitsu
items.blindBackTranslation: Look for Nodules on the Roots

items.sourceEnglish: Legumes work with rhizobia in nodules on their roots.
items.draft: Legumes swi tirha swin'we ni rhizobia eka nodules etimitsini ta swona.
items.blindBackTranslation: Legumes work together with rhizobia at the nodules on their roots.

items.sourceEnglish: Look for Root Nodules
items.draft: Lava Nodules eka Timitsu
items.blindBackTranslation: Look for Nodules on the Roots

items.sourceEnglish: These bacteria convert nitrogen from the air into forms the legume can use.  Find nodules on a spare legume plant. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, suitable bacteria and growing conditions. Can you find the nodules?
items.draft: Magermu (bacteria) lawa ya hundzula nitrogen leyi nga emoyeni yi va swivumbeko leswi legume yi nga swi tirhisaka. Kuma nodules eka ximila xa legume lexi engetelekeke. Nodulation ni ku kula swi titshege hi ximila, bacteria leti faneleke ni swiyimo swa ku kula. Xana u nga kuma nodules?
items.blindBackTranslation: These germs turn nitrogen that is in the air into forms that a legume can use. Find nodules on an extra/additional [?] legume plant. Nodulation and growth depend on the plant, the suitable bacteria and the growing conditions. Can you find nodules?

items.sourceEnglish: Return Leaves to the Soil
items.draft: Tlherisa Matluka Emisaveni
items.blindBackTranslation: Return Leaves to the Soil

items.sourceEnglish: Nitrogen in plant material becomes useful as that material breaks down.
items.draft: Nitrogen leyi nga eka swilo swa swimila yi va ya nkoka loko swilo leswo swi bola.
items.blindBackTranslation: Nitrogen that is in the things of plants becomes important when those things rot.

items.sourceEnglish: Return Leaves to the Soil
items.draft: Tlherisa Matluka Emisaveni
items.blindBackTranslation: Return Leaves to the Soil

items.sourceEnglish: Return suitable leafy prunings, fallen leaves and crop residues as mulch. Soil organisms release nutrients during decomposition.  This takes time. A living legume is not an instant fertiliser pipe into the fruit tree. Which residues can you return?
items.draft: Tlherisa matluka lama tsemiweke lama faneleke, matluka lama wiseke ni swisaleli swa swibyariwa tani hi mulch. Swivumbiwa leswi hanyaka emisaveni swi humesa nutrients hi nkarhi wa decomposition. Leswi swi teka nkarhi. Legume leyi hanyaka a hi payipi ya manyoro ya xihatla leyi yaka eka murhi wa mihandzu. Hi swihi swisaleli leswi u nga swi tlherisaka?
items.blindBackTranslation: Return suitable cut leaves, fallen leaves and the plant residues of crops as mulch. The living things in the soil release nutrients during decomposition. This takes time. A living legume is not a quick fertiliser pipe going to the fruit tree. Which plant residues will you return?

items.sourceEnglish: Sesbania Has a Useful Role
items.draft: Sesbania Yi Ni Ntirho Wa Nkoka
items.blindBackTranslation: Sesbania Has an Important Job

items.sourceEnglish: Sesbania sesban can supply fast growth and leafy mulch.
items.draft: Sesbania sesban yi nga nyika ku kula hi xihatla ni mulch wa matluka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Sesbania sesban can give quick growth and leaf mulch.

items.sourceEnglish: Sesbania Has a Useful Role
items.draft: Sesbania Yi Ni Ntirho Wa Nkoka
items.blindBackTranslation: Sesbania Has an Important Job

items.sourceEnglish: It is indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage this short-lived shrub or small tree as a support plant.  Allow room for its growth. Prune for mulch and reassess it when shade or water competition increases. Where could you manage its growth?
items.draft: Yi indigenous eka KwaZulu-Natal. Eka swiyimo leswi faneleke swa ku fudumala, lawula xihlahla lexi hanyaka nkarhi wo koma kumbe murhi lowutsongo tani hi support plant. Siya ndhawu yo kula ka yona. Tsema marhavi ya yona ku kuma mulch, u tlhela u yi languta nakambe loko ndzhuti kumbe ku lwela mati swi andza. Xana u nga lawula ku kula ka yona kwihi?
items.blindBackTranslation: It is indigenous to KwaZulu-Natal. In suitable warm conditions, manage/control [?] a shrub that lives a short time or a small tree as a support plant. Leave its place of growing [?]. Cut its branches to get mulch, and look at it again when shade or competing for water increases. Where can you control its growth?

items.sourceEnglish: Check the Full Plant Name
items.draft: Kambela Vito Leri Heleleke Ra Ximila
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the Full Name of the Plant

items.sourceEnglish: Sesbania sesban and Sesbania punicea are different species.
items.draft: Sesbania sesban na Sesbania punicea i mixaka leyi hambaneke ya swimila.
items.blindBackTranslation: Sesbania sesban and Sesbania punicea are different kinds of plants.

items.sourceEnglish: Check the Full Plant Name
items.draft: Kambela Vito Leri Heleleke Ra Ximila
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the Full Name of the Plant

items.sourceEnglish: Sesbania punicea is the invasive red sesbania. Its pods have four lengthwise wings. Confirm identity using reliable botanical guidance.  Check the full name before planting. Respect the agreed project species list, including any restriction on Sesbania sesban. Can the supplier verify the species?
items.draft: Sesbania punicea i red sesbania leyi nga invasive. Swikhumba swa yona swa mbewu (pods) swi ni timpapa ta mune leti leha hi ku leha ka swikhumba. Tiyisisa leswaku i xihi hi ku tirhisa botanical guidance leyi tshembekaka. Kambela vito leri heleleke u nga si byala. Xixima project species list leyi pfumeleriweke, ku katsa ku sivela ka xin'wana ni xin'wana eka Sesbania sesban. Xana muphakeri a nga tiyisisa leswaku i xihi ximila?
items.blindBackTranslation: Sesbania punicea is a red sesbania that is invasive. Its seed pods have four wings that are long along the length of the pods. Make sure which it is by using botanical guidance that is trustworthy. Check the full name before you plant. Respect the project species list that has been agreed, including any prevention/restriction on Sesbania sesban. Can the supplier confirm which plant it is?

items.sourceEnglish: Pigeon Pea Gives Food Too
items.draft: Pigeon Pea Na Yona Yi Nyika Swakudya
items.blindBackTranslation: Pigeon Pea Also Gives Food

items.sourceEnglish: Pigeon pea—Cajanus cajan—can provide peas, leafy material and nitrogen fixation.
items.draft: Pigeon pea—Cajanus cajan—yi nga nyika tinyawa, swilo swa matluka ni nitrogen fixation.
items.blindBackTranslation: Pigeon pea—Cajanus cajan—can give peas [?], leaf things and nitrogen fixation.

items.sourceEnglish: Pigeon Pea Gives Food Too
items.draft: Pigeon Pea Na Yona Yi Nyika Swakudya
items.blindBackTranslation: Pigeon Pea Also Gives Food

items.sourceEnglish: Use a sunny, freely draining position. It is a short-lived support shrub; frost and waterlogging can limit it.  Decide whether each plant mainly supplies peas or leafy material. Frequent severe cutting can damage it and reduce the food harvest. Are you growing this plant for peas or mulch?
items.draft: Tirhisa ndhawu leyi nga ni dyambu leyi mati ma hundzaka kahle eka yona. I support shrub leyi hanyaka nkarhi wo koma; frost ni ku tshama ka mati emisaveni swi nga yi hunguta ku kula. Endla xiboho xa leswaku ximila xin'wana ni xin'wana xi nyika ngopfu tinyawa kumbe swilo swa matluka. Ku yi tsema hi matimba minkarhi yo tala swi nga yi vavisa ni ku hunguta ntshovelo wa swakudya. Xana u byala ximila lexi hikwalaho ka tinyawa kumbe mulch?
items.blindBackTranslation: Use a place that has sun and where water passes through well. It is a support shrub that lives for a short time [?]; frost and water standing in the soil can reduce its growth. Make a decision that each plant gives mostly nitrogen or things of leaves [?]. Cutting it hard many times can hurt it and reduce the harvest of food. Are you planting this plant because of nitrogen or mulch?

items.sourceEnglish: Choose for Place and Size
items.draft: Hlawula Hi Ndhawu Ni Vukulu
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose by Site and Size

items.sourceEnglish: A useful support tree in one place may be too large or unsuitable in another.
items.draft: Support tree leyi pfunaka ndhawu yin'wana yi nga va yikulu ngopfu kumbe yi nga faneleki ndhawu yin'wana.
items.blindBackTranslation: A support tree that helps one site can be too big or not suitable for another site.

items.sourceEnglish: Choose for Place and Size
items.draft: Hlawula Hi Ndhawu Ni Vukulu
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose by Site and Size

items.sourceEnglish: Compare mature crown, roots, shade, rainfall and temperature. Check locally appropriate species and planting rules.  Put large support trees where they have space. For a small young guild, a manageable shrub may be easier to maintain. How large will this plant become?
items.draft: Fananisa crown leyi kuleke, timitsu, ndzhuti, mpfula ni ku hisa kumbe ku titimela. Kambela mixaka leyi faneleke ndhawu ya laha ni milawu ya ku byala. Veka support trees leti kulu laha ti nga ni ndhawu. Eka guild yitsongo leyi ntshwa, xihlahla lexi nga lawuleka xi nga olova ku xi hlayisa. Xana ximila lexi xi ta va xikulu ku fika kwihi?
items.blindBackTranslation: Compare a grown crown, roots, shade, rain and heat or shelter [?]. Check the kinds that suit the site here and the rules of planting. Put big support trees where they have space. For a small new guild, a shrub that can be controlled may be easier to look after. How big will this plant become, up to where?

items.sourceEnglish: Annual Cover Has a Place
items.draft: Annual Cover Yi Ni Ndhawu Ya Yona
items.blindBackTranslation: Annual Cover Has Its Place

items.sourceEnglish: Sunn hemp can cover a suitable warm-season gap before the next crop.
items.draft: Sunn hemp yi nga funengeta ndhawu leyi nga riki na swilo hi nkarhi wa ku hisa lowu faneleke, ku nga si va xibyariwa lexi landzelaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Sunn hemp can cover ground that has no things on it during a suitable hot season, before the next crop comes.

items.sourceEnglish: Annual Cover Has a Place
items.draft: Annual Cover Yi Ni Ndhawu Ya Yona
items.blindBackTranslation: Annual Cover Has Its Place

items.sourceEnglish: Grow it where its season and space fit the plan. Its contribution depends on growth, nodulation and the material returned.  After cutting, allow for decomposition. An annual cover crop plays a different role from a longer-lived support shrub. When will this space be needed again?
items.draft: Yi byale laha nkarhi wa yona ni ndhawu swi fambisanaka ni ku hlela. Mpfuno wa yona wu titshege hi ku kula, nodulation ni swilo leswi tlheriseriweke. Endzhaku ka ku yi tsema, siyela nkarhi wa decomposition. Annual cover crop yi endla ntirho wo hambana ni support shrub leyi hanyaka nkarhi wo leha. Xana ndhawu leyi yi ta lavekela rini nakambe?
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant it where its time and place fit with the planning. Its benefit depends on growth, nodulation and the things that are returned. After cutting it, leave time for decomposition. An annual cover crop does a different job from a support shrub that lives a long time. When will this place be needed again?

items.sourceEnglish: Leave Room Around the Tree
items.draft: Siya Ndhawu Ku Rhendzela Murhi
items.blindBackTranslation: Leave Space Around the Tree

items.sourceEnglish: Keep the young fruit tree in light and retain access for care.
items.draft: Hlayisa murhi wa mihandzu lowuntshwa wu ri eka ku vonakala, u tlhela u siya ndlela yo fikelela yo wu hlayisa.
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep the young fruit tree in the sun [visibility], and also leave a way of reaching it to look after it.

items.sourceEnglish: Leave Room Around the Tree
items.draft: Siya Ndhawu Ku Rhendzela Murhi
items.blindBackTranslation: Leave Space Around the Tree

items.sourceEnglish: Keep an open establishment basin and access to the fruit tree. Place temporary support plants where their size and water use can be managed.  Put leafy cuttings where mulch is needed. Neighbouring fruit trees can share support strips between them. Can you reach both plants as they grow?
items.draft: Hlayisa establishment basin yi pfulekile ni ndlela yo fika eka murhi wa mihandzu. Veka support plants ta nkarhi wo koma laha vukulu ni ku tirhisa ka tona mati swi nga lawuriwaka. Veka matluka lama tsemiweke laha mulch yi lavekaka. Mirhi ya mihandzu leyi tshamaka ekusuhi yi nga avelana support strips leti nga exikarhi ka yona. Xana u nga fika eka swimila swimbirhi leswi loko swi ya swi kula?
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep the establishment basin open, with a way to get to the fruit tree. Put short-lived support plants where their size and use of water can be controlled. Put cut leaves where mulch is needed. Fruit trees that stand close by can share support strips that are between them. Can you reach these two plants as they keep growing?

items.sourceEnglish: Build a Layered Support Guild
items.draft: Aka Support Guild Ya Swiyenge (layers)
items.blindBackTranslation: Build a Support Guild Of Layers (layers)

items.sourceEnglish: Combine seasonal cover, support shrubs and temporary small trees.
items.draft: Hlanganisa xifunengeto xa nkarhi wun'wana wa lembe, support shrubs ni mirhi yitsongo ya nkarhi wo koma.
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine a covering of one season of the year, support shrubs and small short-lived trees.

items.sourceEnglish: Build a Layered Support Guild
items.draft: Aka Support Guild Ya Swiyenge
items.blindBackTranslation: Build a Support Guild of Parts

items.sourceEnglish: Cowpea covers sunny gaps. Pigeon pea provides food and leafy material. Managed Sesbania sesban can supply taller temporary support.  Add suitable flowering and mulch plants. Keep the mango trunk clear and manage light, water and access. Which layers fit your site?
items.draft: Cowpea yi funengeta tindhawu leti pfulekeke leti nga ni dyambu. Pigeon pea yi nyika swakudya ni swilo swa matluka. Sesbania sesban leyi lawuriweke yi nga nyika support plant leyi tlakukeke ku tlula swin'wana, ya nkarhi wo koma. Engetela swimila swa swiluva ni swa mulch leswi faneleke. Hlayisa xikhuni xa mango xi nga funengetiwi, u lawula ku vonakala, mati ni ndlela yo fikelela. Hi swihi swiyenge (layers) leswi fambisanaka ni ndhawu ya wena?
items.blindBackTranslation: Cowpea covers open places that have sun. Pigeon pea gives food and leaf things [?: leaf material]. Sesbania sesban that is managed can give a support plant that is raised/taller above the others, of a short time. Add flower plants and suitable mulch plants. Keep the mango trunk not covered, and manage light, water and access (way to reach). Which layers fit together with your place?

items.sourceEnglish: How Many Support Plants?
items.draft: Support Plants Tingani?
items.blindBackTranslation: How many Support Plants?

items.sourceEnglish: Plan abundant support where the site and your care can sustain it.
items.draft: Hlela support plants yo tala laha ndhawu ni vuhlayisi bya wena swi nga swi kondletelaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Plan many support plants where your place and your care can provide for them.

items.sourceEnglish: How Many Support Plants?
items.draft: Support Plants Tingani?
items.blindBackTranslation: How many Support Plants?

items.sourceEnglish: Count woody supports across the spaces between fruit trees. Sow suitable ground cover by area.  There is no universal number per fruit tree. Adjust density to water, soil, plant size and your ability to prune and thin. How much support can you maintain?
items.draft: Hlaya support plants leti nga ni swikhuni eka tindhawu hinkwato leti nga exikarhi ka mirhi ya mihandzu. Byala swimila leswi hangalakaka ehenhla ka misava leswi faneleke hi ku landza vukulu bya ndhawu. A ku na nhlayo yin'we leyi tirhaka eka murhi wun'wana ni wun'wana wa mihandzu. Cincela nhlayo ya swona eka ndhawu yin'wana ni yin'wana hi ku landza mati, misava, vukulu bya ximila ni vuswikoti bya wena bya ku tsema ni thinning. Xana u nga hlayisa support plants tingani?
items.blindBackTranslation: Count the support plants that have wood [?: woody] in all the places that are between the fruit trees. Plant plants that spread above the ground that are suitable according to the size of the place. There is no single number that works for every fruit tree. Change their number in each place according to water, soil, the size of the plant and your ability to cut (prune) and thinning. How many support plants can you keep?

items.sourceEnglish: Chop-and-Drop for Light and Mulch
items.draft: Chop-and-Drop ya Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu na Mulch
items.blindBackTranslation: Chop-and-Drop of Sun Exposure [?] and Mulch

items.sourceEnglish: Watch the branch fall onto the cut leaves.
items.draft: Languta rhavi ri wela ehenhla ka matluka lama tsemiweke.
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch the branch falling above the leaves that were cut.

items.sourceEnglish: Chop-and-Drop for Light and Mulch
items.draft: Chop-and-Drop ya Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu na Mulch
items.blindBackTranslation: Chop-and-Drop of Sun Exposure [?] and Mulch

items.sourceEnglish: Prune a support tree and return suitable leafy cuttings to the soil. The clip shows a branch cut: the support tree remains standing. Leave enough healthy foliage for the plant to recover.  Match cutting to the species. Avoid frequent severe cuts on pigeon pea, especially when growing it for peas. Which plant needs a cut—and how much?
items.draft: Tsema tirhavi ta support tree kutani u vuyisela misava matluka lama faneleke lama tsemiweke. Vhidiyo yi kombisa rhavi leri tsemiweke: support tree yi ha yimile. Siya matluka lama hanyaka lama ringaneke leswaku xibyariwa xi tlhela xi tiyisa. Tsema hi ku ya hi muxaka wa xibyariwa. Papalata ku tsema ngopfu ku phindha-phindha eka pigeon pea, ngopfu-ngopfu loko u yi byala leswaku u kuma mimbewu ya yona leyi dyiwaka (peas). I xibyariwa xihi lexi lavaka ku tsemiwa, naswona ku tsemiwa hi mpimo wihi?
items.blindBackTranslation: Cut the branches of the support tree and return to the soil the suitable leaves that were cut. The video shows a cut branch: the support tree is still standing. Leave enough living leaves so that the crop strengthens again. Cut according to the type of crop. Avoid cutting too much repeatedly on pigeon pea, especially when you plant it to get its edible seeds (peas). Which crop needs cutting, and cutting to what measure?

items.sourceEnglish: Keep Mulch Off the Trunk
items.draft: Hlayisa mulch yi nga khumbi nsinya
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep the mulch from touching the trunk

items.sourceEnglish: Spread suitable cut material over the soil, with the trunk and root collar clear.
items.draft: Hangalasa swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi faneleke ehenhla ka misava, nsinya na root collar swi nga ri na nchumu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Spread the suitable cut things on top of the soil, with the trunk and root collar having nothing on them (left bare).

items.sourceEnglish: Keep Mulch Off the Trunk
items.draft: Hlayisa mulch yi nga khumbi nsinya
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep the mulch from touching the trunk

items.sourceEnglish: Mulch protects the surface, helps conserve moisture and returns organic material.  Leave access for watering and inspection. Cut material into manageable pieces and keep observing moisture and decomposition. Is the root collar still clear?
items.draft: Mulch yi sirhelela ehenhla ka misava, yi pfuna ku hlayisa mati ni ku vuyisela swilo swa organic. Siya ndlela yo cheleta mati ni ku kambela. Tsema swilo leswi tsemiweke swi va swiphemu leswi u nga swi lawulaka, u tlhela u ya emahlweni u languta mati ya le misaveni ni decomposition. Xana root collar yi ha nga ri na nchumu?
items.blindBackTranslation: Mulch protects the top of the soil, helps to keep water and to return organic things. Leave a way to pour water and to check. Cut the cut things into pieces that you can control/manage, and keep going forward looking at the water of the soil and decomposition. Is the root collar still with nothing on it (bare)?

items.sourceEnglish: Choose the Right Comfrey
items.draft: Hlawula Comfrey Leyi Faneleke
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose the Suitable Comfrey

items.sourceEnglish: Bocking 14 comfrey can supply cut leaves for mulch.
items.draft: Bocking 14 comfrey yi nga nyika matluka lama tsemiweke yo endla mulch.
items.blindBackTranslation: Bocking 14 comfrey can give cut leaves for making mulch.

items.sourceEnglish: Choose the Right Comfrey
items.draft: Hlawula Comfrey Leyi Faneleke
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose the Suitable Comfrey

items.sourceEnglish: Obtain the correct cultivar. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but root pieces can regrow.  Place it where it has room and sufficient moisture. Cut leaves as it recovers; do not crowd the young fruit tree. Is this a good permanent place for the clump?
items.draft: Kuma cultivar leyi lulameke. Bocking 14 a yi hangalali hi viable seed, kambe swiphemu swa timitsu swi nga mila nakambe. Yi byale laha ku nga ni ndhawu ni mati lama ringaneke. Tsema matluka loko yi ri karhi yi tlhela yi tiyisa; u nga yi tshiki yi phikizana ni murhi lowuntsongo wa mihandzu. Xana lexi i ndhawu leyinene ya nkarhi hinkwawo ya ku tshama ya xihlopha lexi?
items.blindBackTranslation: Find the right cultivar. Bocking 14 does not spread by viable seed, but pieces of roots can grow again. Plant it where there is space and enough water. Cut the leaves while it is growing and strengthening; do not leave it to compete with the small fruit tree. Is this a good place for the all-the-time sitting [?] (permanent location) of this group?

items.sourceEnglish: Observe Helpful Insects
items.draft: Languta Swinyenyana (insects) Leswi Pfunaka
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch for Helpful Insects

items.sourceEnglish: Flowers can provide resources for useful insects.
items.draft: Swiluva swi nga nyika swihlovo eka swinyenyana (insects) leswi pfunaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Flowers can give sources (of food) to helpful insects.

items.sourceEnglish: Observe Helpful Insects
items.draft: Languta Swinyenyana (insects) Leswi Pfunaka
items.blindBackTranslation: Watch for Helpful Insects

items.sourceEnglish: Many ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack crop pests. Flowering members such as African basil can add resources.  Watch which insects visit and whether damage changes. A flowering plant does not guarantee pest control. What is the insect actually doing?
items.draft: Ladybirds yo tala yi dya aphids; parasitoid wasps yin'wana yi hlasela swinyenyana leswi onhaka swilimo (pests). Swirho leswi nga ni swiluva ku fana na African basil swi nga engetela swihlovo. Languta swinyenyana (insects) leswi endzelaka ni loko ku onhaka ku cinca. Xihlahla lexi nga ni swiluva a xi tiyisekisi ku lawula pests. Xana xinyenyana lexi xi endla yini hakunene?
items.blindBackTranslation: Most ladybirds eat aphids; some parasitoid wasps attack insects that spoil/damage crops. Parts/members that have flowers, like African basil, can add sources. Watch the insects that visit, and whether the damage changes. A plant with flowers does not guarantee control of pests. What does this insect really do?

items.sourceEnglish: Give Flowers Their Space
items.draft: Nyika Swiluva Ndhawu Ya Swona
items.blindBackTranslation: Give Flowers Their Place

items.sourceEnglish: Wild garlic can be a flowering member where the site suits it.
items.draft: Wild garlic yi nga va xirho lexi nga ni swiluva laha ndhawu yi yi fanelaka kona.
items.blindBackTranslation: Wild garlic can be a flowering part/member where the place suits it.

items.sourceEnglish: Give Flowers Their Space
items.draft: Nyika Swiluva Ndhawu Ya Swona
items.blindBackTranslation: Give Flowers Their Place

items.sourceEnglish: Tulbaghia violacea has narrow leaves and lilac flowers. Place a clump where it has light and room to grow.  Observe visiting insects. Do not promise that a ring of wild garlic will repel pests or cure an outbreak. Where can flowers grow without crowding?
items.draft: Tulbaghia violacea yi ni matluka lama nga banzi ni swiluva leswi nga ni muhlovo wa lilac. Byala xihlopha laha ku nga ni ku vonakala ka dyambu ni ndhawu yo kula. Languta swinyenyana (insects) leswi endzelaka. U nga tshembisi leswaku xirhendzevutani xa wild garlic xi ta tlherisela endzhaku swinyenyana leswi onhaka swilimo (pests) kumbe ku herisa ku hangalala ka swona. Xana swiluva swi nga kula kwihi handle ka ku phikizana?
items.blindBackTranslation: Tulbaghia violacea has leaves that are not wide and flowers that have a lilac colour. Plant the group where there is sunlight and room to grow. Look at the small animals/insects that visit. Do not promise that the wild garlic border will drive back the small animals/insects that spoil crops, or stop their spreading. Where can the flowers grow without competing?

items.sourceEnglish: Bring the Jobs Together
items.draft: Hlanganisa Mintirho
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine Functions

items.sourceEnglish: Choose useful partners while protecting the mango's growing space.
items.draft: Hlawula vanghana lava pfunaka loko u sirhelela ndhawu yo kula ya mango.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose helper companions when you protect the growing area of the mango.

items.sourceEnglish: Bring the Jobs Together
items.draft: Hlanganisa Mintirho
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine Functions

items.sourceEnglish: Combine the support functions your site needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and ground cover. Some plants serve several functions.  Keep the trunk area and path open. Reassess each member as the mango and its neighbours grow. Does each member have space and a job?
items.draft: Hlanganisa support functions leswi ndhawu ya wena yi swi lavaka: nitrogen fixation, swakudya, mulch, swiluva ni swimila leswi funengetaka misava. Swihlahla swin'wana swi endla mintirho yo tala. Siya ndhawu ya nsinya ni ndlela swi pfulekile. Kambela nakambe xirho xin'wana ni xin'wana loko mango ni swihlahla leswi tshamaka ekusuhi na yona swi ri karhi swi kula. Xana xirho xin'wana ni xin'wana xi ni ndhawu ni ntirho?
items.blindBackTranslation: Combine the support functions that your place needs: nitrogen fixation, food, mulch, flowers and plants that cover the soil. Some plants do many functions. Leave space for the trunk and a way (path) open. Check again each part/member when the mango and the plants that stay near it are growing. Does each part/member have a place and a function?

items.sourceEnglish: Food Cover Also Competes
items.draft: Xakudya Lexi Funengetaka Na Xona Xa Phikizana
items.blindBackTranslation: Food That Also Covers and Also Competes

items.sourceEnglish: Sweet potato can cover ground and provide food in a suitable sunny space.
items.draft: Sweet potato yi nga funengeta misava yi tlhela yi nyika swakudya endhawini leyi faneleke leyi nga ni dyambu.
items.blindBackTranslation: Sweet potato can cover the soil and give food in a suitable place that has sun.

items.sourceEnglish: Food Cover Also Competes
items.draft: Xakudya Lexi Funengetaka Na Xona Xa Phikizana
items.blindBackTranslation: Food That Also Covers and Also Competes

items.sourceEnglish: Keep its vines away from the young fruit tree and retain a route for care. Its roots also use water and nutrients.  Where resources are tight, compare living cover with an ordinary mulch basin. Is this cover helping the tree establish?
items.draft: Hlayisa marhavi ya yona lama hangalakaka ekule na murhi lowuntsongo wa mihandzu, u tlhela u siya ndlela yo yi hlayisa. Timitsu ta yona na tona ti tirhisa mati ni nutrients. Laha swihlovo swi nga ringani, fananisa swimila leswi hanyaka leswi funengetaka ni mulch basin ya ntolovelo. Xana leswi swimila swi pfuna murhi ku tshama hi ku tiyisa timitsu?
items.blindBackTranslation: Keep its spreading vines far from the small fruit tree, and leave a way to keep/tend it. Its roots also use water and nutrients. Where sources are not enough, compare living plants that cover (the soil) with a normal mulch basin. Do these plants help the tree to stay by making its roots strong?

items.sourceEnglish: First, Establish the Guild
items.draft: Sungula Hi Ku Simekisa Guild
items.blindBackTranslation: Start by Establishing the Guild

items.sourceEnglish: Start while the young fruit tree and its support plants have enough light and water.
items.draft: Sungula loko murhi lowuntsongo wa mihandzu ni support plants ta wona swi ri ni ku vonakala ka dyambu loku ringaneke ni mati lama ringaneke.
items.blindBackTranslation: Start when the small fruit tree and its support plants have enough sunlight and enough water.

items.sourceEnglish: First, Establish the Guild
items.draft: Sungula Hi Ku Simekisa Guild
items.blindBackTranslation: Start by Establishing the Guild

items.sourceEnglish: Plant into a suitable season, mulch and maintain establishment water. Keep the access gap open.  Start with the number of support plants you can care for. Observe survival and growth before adding more. Can you care for every plant through establishment?
items.draft: Byala hi nkarhi lowu faneleke, endla mulch u tlhela u hlayisa mati ya nkarhi wa ku sungula ku tshama endzhaku ka ku byariwa. Siya ndlela yo nghena yi pfulekile. Sungula hi nhlayo ya support plants leyi u nga yi hlayisaka. Languta ku hanya ni ku kula u nga se engetela. Xana u nga hlayisa xihlahla xin'wana ni xin'wana hi nkarhi hinkwawo wa ku sungula ku tshama?
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant at a suitable time, make mulch and keep the water of the time of starting to stay (establishment period) after planting. Leave the entry path open. Start with the number of support plants that you can look after. Watch survival and growth before adding. Can you look after each plant at all times of the establishment period?

items.sourceEnglish: Thin as the Fruit Tree Grows
items.draft: Thinning Loko Murhi Wa Mihandzu Wu Kula
items.blindBackTranslation: Thinning When the Fruit Tree Grows

items.sourceEnglish: When pruning is no longer enough, reduce selected support plants. Cut down selected competing supports to open space. Suitable cut material can stay as mulch: this is thinning through chop-and-drop.  Manage regrowth to keep the opening. Check light, soil moisture and growth; thinning does not instantly stop root competition. Which support plants should now give way?
items.draft: Loko ku tsema tirhavi ku nga ha ringani, hunguta support plants leti hlawuriweke. Tsema ehansi support plants leti phikizanaka leti hlawuriweke leswaku ku pfuleka ndhawu. Swilo leswi tsemiweke leswi faneleke swi nga siyiwa swi ri mulch: leswi i thinning hi chop-and-drop. Lawula ku mila nakambe leswaku ndhawu leyi pfulekeke yi tshama yi ri yona. Kambela ku vonakala ka dyambu, mati ya misava ni ku kula; thinning a yi herisi ku phikizana ka timitsu hi ku hatlisa. I support plants tihi leti nga fanela ku tshika ndhawu sweswi?
items.blindBackTranslation: When cutting of branches is no longer sufficient, reduce the selected support plants. Cut down the selected competing support plants so that space opens up. Cut things that are suitable may be left as mulch: this is thinning by chop-and-drop. Control regrowth so that the opened space stays as it is. Check sunlight, soil water and growth; thinning does not end root competition quickly. Which support plants should give up space now?

items.sourceEnglish: Move Support Into the Light
items.draft: Fambisa Support Plants Eka Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu
items.blindBackTranslation: Move Support Plants To Sun Exposure [?]

items.sourceEnglish: As shade increases, renew sun-loving support plants in open edges and younger plantings.
items.draft: Loko ndzhuti wu engeteleka, tlhela u byala support plants leti rhandzaka dyambu emakumu lama pfulekeke ni eka swibyariwa leswintshwa.
items.blindBackTranslation: When shade increases, plant support plants that like the sun again at the open edges and in the new plantings.

items.sourceEnglish: Move Support Into the Light
items.draft: Fambisa Support Plants Eka Ku Vonakala ka Dyambu
items.blindBackTranslation: Move Support Plants To Sun Exposure [?]

items.sourceEnglish: Carry useful prunings back to established trees. Keep nearby plants only where they still perform well.  Mature fruit trees still need nutrients. Monitor growth, harvest and soil conditions; support plants do not remove that need. Where is the next useful sunny space?
items.draft: Rhwala leswi tsemiweke leswi pfunaka u swi tlherisela eka mirhi leyi simekeke. Hlayisa swihlahla leswi nga ekusuhi ntsena laha swi ha tirhaka kahle kona. Mirhi leyi kuleke ya mihandzu yi ha lava nutrients. Languta ku kula, ntshovelo ni xiyimo xa misava; support plants a swi susi xilaveko lexi. Xana i kwihi ndhawu leyi landzelaka leyi pfunaka leyi nga ni dyambu?
items.blindBackTranslation: Carry the helpful cut things and return them to the established trees. Keep the plants that are near only where they still work well. Grown fruit trees still need nutrients. Watch growth, harvest and the condition of the soil; support plants do not remove that need. Where is the next helpful place that has sun?

items.sourceEnglish: Let Observation Decide
items.draft: Leswi U Swi Vonaka Swi Endle Xiboho
items.blindBackTranslation: What You See Made the Decision

items.sourceEnglish: Keep a short record of how the guild performs.
items.draft: Tsala rhekhodo yo koma ya ndlela leyi guild yi tirhaka ha yona.
items.blindBackTranslation: Write a short record of how the guild works.

items.sourceEnglish: Let Observation Decide
items.draft: Leswi U Swi Vonaka Swi Endle Xiboho
items.blindBackTranslation: What You See Made the Decision

items.sourceEnglish: Check fruit-tree growth, shade, soil moisture, useful harvests and pest damage. Note what was cut, returned or removed.  Use these observations to change the layout and care. A plant earns its place through what it does here. What evidence would make you change the guild?
items.draft: Kambela ku kula ka murhi wa mihandzu, ndzhuti, mati ya misava, ntshovelo lowu pfunaka ni ku onhaka hi swinyenyana leswi onhaka swilimo (pests). Tsala leswi tsemiweke, leswi vuyiseriweke kumbe leswi susiweke. Tirhisa leswi u swi vonaka leswaku u cinca ndlela yo veka ni vuhlayisi. Xihlahla xi kuma ndhawu ya xona hi leswi xi swi endlaka laha. I vumbhoni byihi lebyi nga ku endlaka u cinca guild?
items.blindBackTranslation: Check the growth of the fruit tree, shade, soil water, helpful harvest and the spoiling/damage by insects that damage crops. Write what was cut, what was returned or what was removed. Use what you see to change the way of placing and care. A plant finds its place by what it does here. What evidence is what makes you change the guild?

items.sourceEnglish: Plan One Real Guild
items.draft: Kunguhata Guild Yin'we Ya Ntiyiso
items.blindBackTranslation: Plan One Real Guild

items.sourceEnglish: Choose one fruit tree and mark a layout you can manage.
items.draft: Hlawula murhi wun'we wa mihandzu u tlhela u kombisa ndlela yo vekisa leyi u nga yi lawulaka.
items.blindBackTranslation: Choose one fruit tree and show a way of placing that you can control.

items.sourceEnglish: Plan One Real Guild
items.draft: Kunguhata Guild Yin'we Ya Ntiyiso
items.blindBackTranslation: Plan One Real Guild

items.sourceEnglish: Record the tree, site conditions and missing jobs. Name the support species fully, mark the starting number and leave access.  Write down what will trigger pruning or thinning. Agree the species list with the project team where required. Can someone else explain your plan back to you?
items.draft: Tsala murhi, swiyimo swa ndhawu ni mintirho leyi pfumalaka. Thya mavito ya support species hi ku helela, kombisa nhlayo yo sungula u tlhela u siya ndlela yo nghena. Tsala leswi nga ta endla leswaku ku tsemiwa tirhavi kumbe thinning. Pfumelelana hi species list ni ntlawa wa phurojeke laha swi lavekaka kona. Xana munhu un'wana a nga ku hlamuselela nakambe pulani ya wena?
items.blindBackTranslation: Write the tree, the season of the place and the missing tasks [?]. List the names of the support species completely, show the starting number and also leave a way in/entrance [?]. Write what will make pruning of branches or thinning happen. Agree on the species list with the project group where it is needed. Could someone explain your plan to you again?

items.sourceEnglish: Plant, Observe, Adjust
items.draft: Byala, Languta, Cinca
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant, Watch, Change

items.sourceEnglish: Start one suitable guild and care for it through its first stage.
items.draft: Sungula guild yin'we leyi faneleke, u yi hlayisa ku fika emakumu ka nkarhi wa yona wo sungula.
items.blindBackTranslation: Start one suitable guild, and look after it until the end of its starting time.

items.sourceEnglish: Plant, Observe, Adjust
items.draft: Byala, Languta, Cinca
items.blindBackTranslation: Plant, Watch, Change

items.sourceEnglish: Use the right species, a manageable number of plants and room to grow. Return useful biomass and protect the fruit tree.  Review the planting as crowns expand. Keep, cut, replace or remove each support plant when its role changes. What will you do first—and when will you review it?
items.draft: Tirhisa species leyi faneleke, nhlayo leyi nga lawuriwaka ya swimila ni ndhawu yo kula. Vuyisa biomass leyi pfunaka u tlhela u sirhelela murhi wa mihandzu. Kambela nakambe ku byala loko crowns ti ri karhi ti anama. Hlayisa, tsema, cinca hi yin'wana kumbe susa support plant yin'wana ni yin'wana loko ntirho wa yona wu cinca. I yini leswi u nga ta swi endla ku sungula, naswona u ta yi kambela nakambe rini?
items.blindBackTranslation: Use suitable species, a controllable number of plants and space to grow. Return helpful biomass and also protect the fruit tree. Check planting again when crowns are spreading. Keep, cut, change to another or remove each support plant when its job changes. What will you do to start, and when will you check it again?
